title: Choosing when to leave
summary: In R.E.P.O. leaving is a choice you make with the loot in your hands: the game records completed extractions and marks points of interest on the level so a crew can decide when the haul is enough.
body: Finishing is recorded rather than assumed, so a crew that banks an extraction has progress that a crew still inside does not.
The level points the way to places of interest, which is why finding the way out is a navigation task rather than a memory test.
Because the level decides what loot it holds, the question is never whether more exists but whether what is left is worth the risk.
What this entry does not tell you: quotas, payout maths or deadlines. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Completed extractions are recorded by the game.
The level interface works from defined points of interest.
The level decides which valuables are available to take.
Some level behaviour is driven by settings of its own.
